learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the dynamic life cycle of a cell! Learn how cells divide to grow, reproduce, communicate with each other, and eventually die.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The sequence of events a cell goes through to grow and divide. It includes Interphase (G1, S phase where DNA replicates, and G2) and the M phase (Mitosis/division).
Used for growth and repair. One parent cell divides to form two identical daughter cells with the exact same number of chromosomes (diploid). Phases: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.

Used to produce gametes (sperm and eggs). One parent cell undergoes two rounds of division to produce four non-identical daughter cells, each with half the chromosomes (haploid). Crossing over occurs here, causing genetic variation.

Cells communicate using chemical signals (ligands) that bind to specific receptors on the cell surface. This triggers a cascade of reactions inside the cell (signal transduction) leading to a response.
Apoptosis is 'programmed cell death'—a clean, organized way for the body to remove old or damaged cells. Necrosis is messy, unplanned cell death caused by injury or poison, which causes inflammation.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The DNA Halving Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Take a deck of 46 cards (representing human chromosomes). For Mitosis, photocopy the whole deck so you have two decks of 46. For Meiosis, deal the deck into two piles of 23. You just made gametes!

exam_tips: 📌 Remember that DNA replication only occurs during the 'S phase' of interphase, NOT during actual mitosis.
📌 Metaphase is the best stage to study chromosome morphology because chromosomes align perfectly at the cell's equator.
📌 Crossing over (exchange of genetic material) happens in Prophase I of Meiosis I (specifically the Pachytene stage). This is why you don't look exactly like your siblings!
quick_recap: ⭐ The cell cycle has checkpoints to ensure DNA is not damaged before dividing. Cancer occurs when these checkpoints fail.
⭐ Mitosis keeps chromosome numbers constant; Meiosis halves them for sexual reproduction.
⭐ Cell signaling is like a biological postal service, ensuring organs and tissues coordinate their activities.
